analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction that an ISA transfer took six weeks against a stated 15 working days and alleges financial loss of about £56 in interest, which meets CH-1.
analysis.summary: [PERSON_1] complains that an ISA transfer in from another provider took about six weeks, although the bank said it would take 15 working days. The handler's note records that the transfer was received on 03/09 and completed on 15/10. The customer estimates lost interest of about £56 and asks the bank to 'sort it'. No vulnerability indicators were noted. The customer prefers email but also gave a mobile number. The estimated loss is under £100 and there are no escalation triggers, so the complaints handler can deal with this directly. The lost-interest calculation still needs to be verified.

timeline.event: ISA transfer in received by the bank
Handler noted transfer dates, SLA of 15 working days, no vulnerability, email preference

analysis.severity_reason: The customer estimates a loss of about £56, which is under £100. This is a service delay with no fraud, no vulnerability, no legal threat and no repeated contact, so it is Low under CH-6.

vulnerability.suggested_support: No indicators were found in the complaint. The note says 'no vuln' but does not record that the customer was asked. Stay alert for any indicators in further contact.

analysis.routing_reason: None of the ESC-1 triggers apply: there is no fraud, lending, vulnerability referral, systemic issue or technical failure needing investigation. The complaints handler should resolve this.
